Seventeenth
sĕv´en-tēnth
adj. (the ordinal of seventeen; rendering Hebrew sheva esreh)
Old English seofontēotha. The flood began and the ark came to rest on a seventeenth day, five months apart to the day.

Biblical Definition

“In the six hundredth year of Noah's life, in the second month, the seventeenth day of the month, the same day were all the fountains of the great deep broken up” (Gen 7:11); “And the ark rested in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, upon the mountains of Ararat” (Gen 8:4). Ahaziah began to reign over Israel “the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat” (1Ki 22:51), and Ahaz over Judah “in the seventeenth year of Pekah” (2Ki 16:1). The seventeenth lot of the priests fell to Hezir (1Ch 24:15).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines seventeenth as the ordinal of seventeen; the seventh after the tenth.

expand to see more

SEVENTEENTH, a. The ordinal of seventeen; the seventh after the tenth.

Key Scripture

Gen 7:11 — "In the six hundredth year of Noah's life, in the second month, the seventeenth day of the month, the same day were all the fountains of the great deep broken up, and the windows of heaven were opened."

Gen 8:4 — "And the ark rested in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, upon the mountains of Ararat."

1Ki 22:51 — "Ahaziah the son of Ahab began to reign over Israel in Samaria the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and reigned two years over Israel."

2Ki 16:1 — "In the seventeenth year of Pekah the son of Remaliah Ahaz the son of Jotham king of Judah began to reign."

Modern Corruption

The flood is read as legend, and the record keeps a log by the day of the month.

expand to see more

Genesis 7 and 8 are written like a ship's log. The rain began on the seventeenth day of the second month; the waters prevailed a hundred and fifty days; the ark grounded on the seventeenth day of the seventh month — five months of thirty days, to the day. Legends do not keep dates, and the men who call the flood a myth have to explain why the myth has a calendar. The precision is the point: Moses is recording an event that happened to real people in a real year, and Peter builds a warning on it — the world that then was, being overflowed with water, perished, and the heavens and the earth which are now are kept in store (2Pe 3:6–7). A judgment with a date is a judgment that can be believed in, and the next one has a day appointed too.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew sheva esreh (H7651, H6240), seventeen, seventeenth.

expand to see more

Hebrew sheva esreh (H7651 with H6240) — seventeenth; Genesis 7:11, 8:4, 1 Kings 22:51, 2 Kings 16:1, 1 Chronicles 24:15.

Usage

"“The seventeenth day of the month, the same day were all the fountains of the great deep broken up” — the flood dated."

"“On the seventeenth day of the month, upon the mountains of Ararat” — the ark grounded five months later, to the day."

"“The seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat” — the reigns cross-dated."
